t: Formed in 1230 when Ferdinand III united Castile and León, it took Córdoba and Seville and left Granada as the last Muslim state.
Merino wool marketed by the Mesta, the Cortes and Alfonso X's Siete Partidas shaped its economy and law.
Under Isabella I it took Granada and sponsored Columbus, and its laws and language spread across the Spanish Americas.
dyk: The Alfonsine Tables, astronomical tables compiled at the court of Alfonso X in Toledo, remained a standard reference for European astronomers until the sixteenth century.
ev: Ferdinand III inherits León, uniting it permanently with Castile
Seville surrenders to Ferdinand III after a siege of more than a year
Alfonso XI defeats the Marinids and Granada at the Battle of Río Salado
Henry of Trastámara kills Peter I at Montiel and founds a new dynasty
Granada falls, the Jews are expelled and Columbus sails for the Indies
The Comuneros are defeated at the Battle of Villalar
The Nueva Planta decrees begin imposing Castilian institutions on Aragon

f.capital: Itinerant court (Burgos, Toledo, Valladolid, Seville); Madrid from 1561
f.predecessor: Kingdom of Castile; Kingdom of León
